input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 binds us as well as RadialSpark. It already meets most of the fallback: it is mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, capped at one year post-termination, and is solicitation-based rather than a no-hire. However, it contains no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches, which the rule treats as a required element of an acceptable non-solicit; as drafted, ordinary recruiting activity or an inbound approach from a RadialSpark consultant could breach it. We therefore added the customary carve-out sentence only, leaving duration and scope untouched (fallback level, given the mutual bargain already struck).

proposal.summary: Add customary general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicitation clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The mutual non-solicit is otherwise acceptable in duration and scope, so we have only added the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches, consistent with our playbook position that non-solicits must not capture hires we did not target.

ops.oldText: which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: which shall not be unreasonably withheld. This restriction shall not apply to general advertisements or other recruiting efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to the hiring of any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis.
